s0003.literal: Zong Yuanrao; Sima Shen; Mao Xi; Cai Zheng
s0003.idiomatic: Zong Yuanrao; Sima Shen; Mao Xi; Cai Zheng

s0004.literal: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief and placed in charge of the five rites.
s0004.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor-in-chief and placed in charge of the five rites.

s0005.literal: At that time Hezhou Inspector Chen Pou's corruption was notorious; he sent agents to the fisheries to collect fish and further begged rice in six commanderies—the people suffered greatly.
s0005.idiomatic: At that time Hezhou inspector Chen Pou's corruption was notorious; he sent agents to the fisheries to collect fish and further begged rice in six commanderies, and the people suffered greatly.

s0006.literal: Yuanrao impeached and memorialized, saying: "Your servant has heard that raising banners to seek out affliction truly relies on integrity and fairness; drawing aside the carriage curtain to comfort the hidden truly relies on humaneness and forbearance.
s0006.idiomatic: Yuanrao impeached and memorialized: "I have heard that raising banners to seek out affliction truly relies on integrity and fairness; drawing aside the carriage curtain to comfort the hidden truly relies on humaneness and forbearance.

s0007.literal: If greed and corruption are indulged and levies never satisfied, though Heaven's net may be sparse, it will not let this slip through.
s0007.idiomatic: If greed and corruption are indulged and levies never satisfied, though Heaven's net may be sparse, it will not let this slip through.

s0008.literal: Your servant respectfully accuses Marquis of Opening State of Zhongling county, Hezhou Inspector Chen Pou: by many strokes of fortune he met early selection; rank came by grace, office by private favor—without merit or worth he sat atop glory and wealth.
s0008.idiomatic: I respectfully accuse Marquis of Opening State of Zhongling county, Hezhou inspector Chen Pou: by many strokes of fortune he met early selection; rank came by grace, office by private favor—without merit or worth he sat atop glory and wealth.

s0009.literal: The lands of Qiao and Fei had long fallen away; when imperial might recovered them, all looked up to the wind of benevolence.
s0009.idiomatic: The lands of Qiao and Fei had long fallen away; when imperial might recovered them, all looked up to the wind of benevolence.

s0010.literal: A new domain should be ruled lightly and still more awaits generous favor; to be made shepherd here is a charge of special weight.
s0010.idiomatic: A new domain should be ruled lightly and still more awaits generous favor; to be made shepherd here is a charge of special weight.

s0011.literal: Then bending grace descended; he was seen off at the Xuan Chamber and personally received admonition—in the affair equal to having his ear pulled.
s0011.idiomatic: Then bending grace descended; he was seen off at the Xuan Chamber and personally received admonition—in the affair equal to having his ear pulled.

s0012.literal: Though his mind of integrity was not long stored up, having received this stern instruction he could have sharpened his spirit.
s0012.idiomatic: Though his mind of integrity was not long stored up, having received this stern instruction he could have sharpened his spirit.

s0013.literal: Yet he presumptuously imposed levies, monopolized greed and seizure, sought grain without limit—shaming Wang Chen's going out with relief grain; collected fish without bound—differing from Yang Xu's hanging up dried fish; to place him under severe penalty is truly bright law.
s0013.idiomatic: Yet he presumptuously imposed levies, monopolized greed and seizure, sought grain without limit—shaming Wang Chen's going out with relief grain; collected fish without bound—differing from Yang Xu's hanging up dried fish; to place him under severe penalty is truly bright law.

s0014.literal: Your servants jointly deliberate and ask that, according to the decree, Pou be deprived of every office he ought to recover or be exempted from; those who ought to be barred from office and future candidates demoted in original rank—all according to the law for dismissal from office."
s0014.idiomatic: We jointly deliberate and ask that, according to the decree, Pou be deprived of every office he ought to recover or be exempted from; those who ought to be barred from office and future candidates demoted in original rank—all according to the law for dismissal from office."

s0016.literal: Wuxing Administrator Prince of Wuling Wang Bolü and Yuzhang Interior Administrator Prince of Nankang Fang Tai were both arrogant and overbearing; Yuanrao impeached them by memorial and both were stripped and demoted.
s0016.idiomatic: Wuxing administrator Wang Bolü, Prince of Wuling, and Yuzhang interior administrator Fang Tai, Prince of Nankang, were both arrogant and overbearing; Yuanrao impeached them by memorial and both were stripped and demoted.

s0017.literal: Yuanrao's nature was fair and equitable; he was skilled at holding to law, versed in precedent, and bright in the substance of governance; whenever officials broke the law, policy harmed the people, or matters of name and teaching fell short, he corrected them as the case required, with much benefit.
s0017.idiomatic: Yuanrao's nature was fair and equitable; he was skilled at holding to law, versed in precedent, and bright in the substance of governance; whenever officials broke the law, policy harmed the people, or matters of name and teaching fell short, he corrected them as the case required, with much benefit.

s0018.literal: Promoted to General of Firm Prestige and Interior Administrator of Nankang; he used three thousand-odd piculs of his salary grain to assist the people's rent and taxes, inquired after the aged, and rescued the destitute—the people relied on him greatly.
s0018.idiomatic: Promoted to general of firm prestige and interior administrator of Nankang, he used more than three thousand piculs of his salary grain to assist the people's rent and taxes, inquired after the aged, and rescued the destitute—the people relied on him greatly.

s0019.literal: For outstanding administration he entered court; an edict added him as Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and Grand Rectifier of the five provinces Jing, Yong, Xiang, Ba, and Wu.
s0019.idiomatic: For outstanding administration he entered court; an edict added him as scattered-cavalry regular attendant and grand rectifier of Jing, Yong, Xiang, Ba, and Wu.

s0020.literal: Soon he again held his former office and additionally led Left Director of the Masters of Writing for the People.
s0020.idiomatic: Soon he again held his former office and additionally led left director of the masters of writing for the people.

s0022.literal: He passed through Minister of the Left for the People, General of the Right Guard, and leading forward general, and was promoted to Minister of the Masters of Writing for Personnel.
s0022.idiomatic: He passed through minister of the left for the people, general of the right guard, and leading forward general, and was promoted to minister of the masters of writing for personnel.

s0023.literal: In the thirteenth year of Taijian he died, aged sixty-four.
s0023.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Taijian (581) he died, aged sixty-four.

s0024.literal: An edict posthumously made him Palace Attendant and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with officials supplying the funeral.
s0024.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him palace attendant and grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon, with officials supplying the funeral.

s0025.literal: Sima Shen, styled Jihe, was a native of Wen in Henei commandery.
s0025.idiomatic: Sima Shen, styled Jihe, came from Wen in Henei commandery.

s0026.literal: His grandfather Huiyuan was Liang's commissioner of waterways.
s0026.idiomatic: His grandfather Huiyuan was Liang's commissioner of waterways.

s0027.literal: His father Xuantong was Liang's Left Director in the Masters of Writing for the People.
s0027.idiomatic: His father Xuantong was Liang's left director in the masters of writing for the people.

s0028.literal: Shen from early on had presence of spirit; at fourteen he was already skilled at weiqi. He once followed his father to call on the Minister of Personnel, Dao
s0028.idiomatic: Shen from early on had presence of spirit; at fourteen he was already skilled at weiqi. He once followed his father to call on the minister of personnel, Dao

s0030.literal: Collation variant: (Gai), Editorial footnote marker 1. At that time Liang Inspector of Liangzhou Yin Zichun and Director of the Palace Guard Zhu Yi were present.
s0030.idiomatic: Collation variant: (Gai), [1] At that time Liang inspector of Liangzhou Yin Zichun and director of the palace guard Zhu Yi were present.

s0031.literal: Zichun had long known Shen and immediately at the gathering called him to play a match, Editorial footnote marker 2. Shen had fine conceptions each time; Yi watched and marveled, and thereafter drew Shen into his company.
s0031.idiomatic: Zichun had long known Shen and immediately at the gathering called him to play a match, [2] Shen had fine conceptions each time; Yi watched and marveled, and thereafter drew Shen into his company.

s0032.literal: When Liang's Prince of Shaoling served as governor of Danyang, he made Shen his chief clerk.
s0032.idiomatic: When Liang's Prince of Shaoling served as governor of Danyang, he made Shen his chief clerk.

s0033.literal: When the Taqing turmoil came, both his parents died; on this account he vowed to himself and ate vegetables for life.
s0033.idiomatic: When the Taqing turmoil came, both his parents died; on this account he vowed to himself and ate vegetables for life.

s0034.literal: When Liang's Emperor Yuan assumed the provisional mandate, Shen was summoned as General Who Opens the Distance and promoted to recorder in the outer military staff of the Army on the Western Wall.
s0034.idiomatic: When Liang's Emperor Yuan assumed the provisional mandate, Shen was summoned as general who opens the distance and promoted to recorder in the outer military staff of the army on the western wall.

s0035.literal: When Hou Jing attacked Yingzhou, Shen followed Commander Wang Sengbian in holding Baling; every plan he advanced was adopted.
s0035.idiomatic: When Hou Jing attacked Yingzhou, Shen followed commander Wang Sengbian in holding Baling; every plan he advanced was adopted.

s0036.literal: Sengbian sighed and said: "This man wants the saddle and a sweating horse—perhaps not his strength; if one had him pacify troops and hold a city, there would surely be extraordinary achievement.
s0036.idiomatic: Sengbian sighed and said, "This man wants the saddle and a sweating horse—perhaps not his strength; if one had him pacify troops and hold a city, there would surely be extraordinary achievement.

s0037.literal: When Sengbian campaigned against Lu Na, Shen was in the army; at that time the rebel masses suddenly arrived, those left and right were scattered; Shen personally shielded Sengbian, covered himself with a shield and went forward; when Pei Zhiheng's rescue arrived, the rebels then withdrew. Sengbian looked back at Shen and laughed, saying: "The humane surely have courage—is this an empty saying!
s0037.idiomatic: When Sengbian campaigned against Lu Na, Shen was in the army; at that time the rebel masses suddenly arrived and those left and right were scattered; Shen personally shielded Sengbian, covered himself with a shield and went forward; when Pei Zhiheng's rescue arrived, the rebels withdrew. Sengbian looked back at Shen and laughed, saying, "The humane surely have courage—is this an empty saying!

s0038.literal: He was made Scattered Cavalry Attendant.

s0039.literal: At the beginning of Shaotai, he was promoted to Retainer to Hou Andu with ceremonial parity to the Three Offices.
s0039.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shaotai, he was promoted to retainer to Hou Andu with ceremonial parity to the three offices.

s0040.literal: When the Founder took the throne, Shen was made advising officer in the establishment of Pacification East Prince of Linchuan.
s0040.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, Shen was made advising officer in the establishment of Pacification East Prince of Linchuan.

s0041.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng, he was promoted to advising officer of the Northern Expedition and concurrently supervisor of the Court of Ceremonial Rites.
s0041.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiancheng (562), he was promoted to advising officer of the northern expedition and concurrently supervisor of the court of ceremonial rites.

s0042.literal: In year 5, he was made advising officer of the Eastern Expedition and concurrently initiating officer in the Masters of Writing.
s0042.idiomatic: In year 5, he was made advising officer of the eastern expedition and concurrently initiating officer in the masters of writing.

s0043.literal: He went out as General of Martial Splendor and magistrate of Jiangcheng—his governance had outstanding results.
s0043.idiomatic: He went out as general of martial splendor and magistrate of Jiangcheng; his governance had outstanding results.

s0044.literal: He entered court as Gold Section Director in the Masters of Writing.
s0044.idiomatic: He entered court as gold section director in the masters of writing.

s0045.literal: He was promoted to Director for the People on the left; removed from office for public affairs.
s0045.idiomatic: He was promoted to director for the people on the left and removed from office for public affairs.

s0046.literal: At the beginning of Taijian he was summoned as General of Firm Prestige and advising officer of the Southern Expedition Prince of Poyang.
s0046.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taijian he was summoned as general of firm prestige and advising officer of the southern expedition Prince of Poyang.

s0047.literal: In year 9, he was made magistrate of Moling; in office he was recorded for integrity and ability, and a white sparrow nested in the county courtyard.
s0047.idiomatic: In year 9, he was made magistrate of Moling; in office he was recorded for integrity and ability, and a white sparrow nested in the county courtyard.

s0048.literal: When his term ended, shortly thereafter he joined the eastern-palace guest staff; soon he also served concurrently as eastern-palace communicating affairs attendant.
s0048.idiomatic: When his term ended, shortly thereafter he joined the eastern-palace guest staff; soon he also served concurrently as eastern-palace communicating affairs attendant.

s0049.literal: Promoted to Extraordinary Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, attendant post as before.
s0049.idiomatic: Promoted to extraordinary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, attendant post as before.

s0050.literal: When Shuling's violent outrage took place, the affair did not succeed and he went out to hold the eastern palace; Shen galloped to summon Right Guard Xiao Mohe to lead troops and arrive first, pursued and beheaded him, then entered the city and seized his treasury stores—Houzhu deeply commended him.
s0050.idiomatic: When Shuling's violent outrage took place, the affair did not succeed and he went out to hold the eastern palace; Shen galloped to summon right guard Xiao Mohe to lead troops and arrive first, pursued and beheaded him, then entered the city and seized his treasury stores—Houzhu deeply commended him.

s0051.literal: For his merit he was made Left Leader of the Heir Apparent's Guard, enfeoffed as Wen
s0051.idiomatic: For his merit he was made left leader of the heir apparent's guard, enfeoffed as Wen

s0053.literal: Collation variant: (Zhao) County Baron, Editorial footnote marker 3. fief four hundred households, and concurrently Secretariat Communicating Affairs Attendant.
s0053.idiomatic: Collation variant: (Zhao) county baron, [3] fief four hundred households, and concurrently secretariat communicating affairs attendant.

s0054.literal: Soon he was promoted to General of the Right Guard, with additional Unimpeded Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant.
s0054.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to general of the right guard, with additional unimpeded scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

s0055.literal: Because of illness he returned to his residence; he was then given additional Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, with right guard and attendant posts as before.
s0055.idiomatic: Because of illness he returned to his residence; he was then given additional scattered-cavalry regular attendant, with right guard and attendant posts as before.

s0056.literal: In the fourth year of Zhide he died; Houzhu mourned him long and issued an edict saying: "Care in the end and remembrance of the distant, reverence for old norms, closing the coffin and fixing the posthumous title—these suppress former canons.
s0056.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhide (586) he died; Houzhu mourned him long and issued an edict: "Care in the end and remembrance of the distant, reverence for old norms, closing the coffin and fixing the posthumous title—these suppress former canons.

s0057.literal: The late Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, General of the Right Guard, Wen
s0057.idiomatic: The late scattered-cavalry regular attendant, general of the right guard, Wen

s0059.literal: Collation variant: (Zhao) County Founding Baron Shen was loyal and solemn in public service, pure and upright in his person, governing complexity with restraint and casting his body to follow righteousness.
s0059.idiomatic: Collation variant: (Zhao) county founding baron Shen was loyal and solemn in public service, pure and upright in his person, governing complexity with restraint and casting his body to follow righteousness.

s0060.literal: We entrusted him with deep feeling and were about to bring peace to the people's labors; suddenly he transformed and went—grief pierces the breast.
s0060.idiomatic: We entrusted him with deep feeling and were about to bring peace to the people's labors; suddenly he transformed and went—grief pierces the breast.

s0061.literal: He may be posthumously made Palace Attendant and Protector General, his rank advanced to marquis, his fief increased to five hundred households, posthumous title Zhong.
s0061.idiomatic: He may be posthumously made palace attendant and protector general, his rank advanced to marquis, his fief increased to five hundred households, posthumous title Zhong.

s0062.literal: Give one set of court robes, one suit of garments; fix a day for mourning; whatever the funeral requires, supply as needed."
s0062.idiomatic: Give one set of court robes, one suit of garments; fix a day for mourning; whatever the funeral requires, supply as needed."

s0063.literal: At the burial Houzhu himself composed the epitaph inscription; the words were painfully moving.
s0063.idiomatic: At the burial Houzhu himself composed the epitaph inscription; the words were painfully moving.

s0065.literal: Heaven does not grant good fortune—it destroys my fine minister.
s0065.idiomatic: Heaven does not grant good fortune—it destroys my fine minister.

s0066.literal: Such was the favor shown him.
s0066.idiomatic: Such was the favor shown him.

s0067.literal: Shen served three emperors and inwardly held confidential affairs; even in hurried moments, on great affairs of army and state, his direction and decisions had no delay.
s0067.idiomatic: Shen served three emperors and inwardly held confidential affairs; even in hurried moments, on great affairs of army and state, his direction and decisions had no delay.

s0068.literal: His son Xiu succeeded him and rose to eastern-palace attendant.
s0068.idiomatic: His son Xiu succeeded him and rose to eastern-palace attendant.

s0069.literal: Mao Xi, styled Bowu, was a native of Yangwu in Xingyang commandery.
s0069.idiomatic: Mao Xi, styled Bowu, came from Yangwu in Xingyang commandery.

s0070.literal: His grandfather Cheng was Liang's Scattered Cavalry Attendant.
s0070.idiomatic: His grandfather Cheng was Liang's scattered-cavalry attendant.

s0071.literal: His father Qizhong was Liang's Director in the Masters of Writing for Comparison and Central Authority Army Major.
s0071.idiomatic: His father Qizhong was Liang's director in the masters of writing for comparison and central authority army major.

s0072.literal: Emperor Wen once told Emperor Xuan: "All my sons take 'Bo' in their names; your sons should use 'Shu' in their style."
s0072.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once told Emperor Xuan, "All my sons take 'Bo' in their names; your sons should use 'Shu' in their style."

s0073.literal: Emperor Xuan consulted Xi; Xi at once listed more than twenty famous men of antiquity such as Du Shuying and Yu Shuqing and reported them to Emperor Wen, and Emperor Wen praised it.
s0073.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan consulted Xi; Xi at once listed more than twenty famous men of antiquity such as Du Shuying and Yu Shuqing and reported them to Emperor Wen, and Emperor Wen praised it.

s0074.literal: When Emperor Wen died, the Deposed Emperor was young and ignorant; Emperor Xuan assumed the recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing as regent; Vice Director Dao Zhongju and others knew that court expectation had a direction and therefore forged an empress dowager order sending Emperor Xuan back to the eastern palace; at the time there was doubt and fear, and none dared speak.
s0074.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen died, the Deposed Emperor was young and ignorant; Emperor Xuan assumed the recorded affairs of the masters of writing as regent; vice director Dao Zhongju and others knew that court expectation had a direction and therefore forged an empress dowager order sending Emperor Xuan back to the eastern palace; at the time there was doubt and fear, and none dared speak.

s0075.literal: Xi at once galloped in and told Emperor Xuan: "Chen has held the realm only a short time; within the seas it is not yet pacified; moreover national misfortune has struck together, and the myriad states are in peril and fear.
s0075.idiomatic: Xi at once galloped in and told Emperor Xuan, "Chen has held the realm only a short time; within the seas it is not yet pacified; moreover national misfortune has struck together, and the myriad states are in peril and fear.

s0076.literal: The empress dowager deeply weighs the plan for the altars of soil and grain and has ordered the prince to enter the Secretariat; we should together bring peace to the people's labors and match the virtue of Yi and Zhou.
s0076.idiomatic: The empress dowager deeply weighs the plan for the altars of soil and grain and has ordered the prince to enter the secretariat; we should together bring peace to the people's labors and match the virtue of Yi and Zhou.

s0077.literal: Today's words surely are not the empress dowager's intent.
s0077.idiomatic: Today's words surely are not the empress dowager's intent.

s0078.literal: The weight of the ancestral altars—please add further thought.
s0078.idiomatic: The weight of the ancestral altars—please add further thought.

s0079.literal: In my foolishness I must hear the matter reported again, and not let treacherous villains carry out their plot."
s0079.idiomatic: In my foolishness I must hear the matter reported again, and not let treacherous villains carry out their plot."

s0080.literal: It turned out as he had planned.
s0080.idiomatic: It turned out as he had planned.

s0081.literal: Right Guard General Han Zigao at first conspired with Zhongju; the affair had not yet broken out; Xi asked Emperor Xuan: "You should select men and horses, assign them to Zigao, and also grant iron and charcoal so he may repair weapons and armor."
s0081.idiomatic: Right guard general Han Zigao at first conspired with Zhongju; the affair had not yet broken out; Xi asked Emperor Xuan, "You should select men and horses, assign them to Zigao, and also grant iron and charcoal so he may repair weapons and armor."

s0082.literal: Emperor Xuan was startled and said: "Zigao plots rebellion—we should at once seize him; why do this further?"
s0082.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was startled and said, "Zigao plots rebellion—we should at once seize him; why do this further?"

s0083.literal: Xi replied: "The imperial tomb has only just been completed and border enemies are still many; Zigao was entrusted by the former court and is known as holding to obedience, yet he is very frivolous and impetuous—I fear he will not promptly surrender his head; if we hasten to punish him, we may transgress royal measure.
s0083.idiomatic: Xi replied, "The imperial tomb has only just been completed and border enemies are still many; Zigao was entrusted by the former court and is known as holding to obedience, yet he is very frivolous and impetuous—I fear he will not promptly surrender his head; if we hasten to punish him, we may transgress royal measure.

s0084.literal: You should push aside suspicion and peacefully entice him so he does not doubt himself; to take him is the strength of one stout warrior."
s0084.idiomatic: You should push aside suspicion and peacefully entice him so he does not doubt himself; to take him is the strength of one stout warrior."

s0085.literal: Emperor Xuan deeply approved and in the end carried out the plan.
s0085.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan deeply approved and in the end carried out the plan.

s0086.literal: When the mass of armies marched north and gained the lands south of the Huai, Xi presented methods for securing the border; Emperor Xuan adopted them and put them into effect that very day.
s0086.idiomatic: When the mass of armies marched north and gained the lands south of the Huai, Xi presented methods for securing the border; Emperor Xuan adopted them and put them into effect that very day.

s0087.literal: He again asked Xi: "I wish to advance troops to Peng and Bian—what do you think?"
s0087.idiomatic: He again asked Xi, "I wish to advance troops to Peng and Bian—what do you think?"

s0088.literal: Xi replied: "Your servant's talent is truly not that of the wise; how would I dare to foretell what has not yet happened?
s0088.idiomatic: Xi replied, "My talent is truly not that of the wise; how would I dare to foretell what has not yet happened?

s0089.literal: I privately think that south of the Huai has only just been pacified and the border people are not yet settled; Zhou has only begun to swallow Qi and is hard to contend with in the blade—how could one with worn troops and weary soldiers press the advance further?
s0089.idiomatic: I privately think that south of the Huai has only just been pacified and the border people are not yet settled; Zhou has only begun to swallow Qi and is hard to contend with in the blade—how could one with worn troops and weary soldiers press the advance further?

s0090.literal: Moreover to abandon the craft of boats and oars and tread the ground of chariots and horses is to leave the long for the short—not what men of Wu find convenient.
s0090.idiomatic: Moreover to abandon the craft of boats and oars and tread the ground of chariots and horses is to leave the long for the short—not what men of Wu find convenient.

s0091.literal: In your servant's foolish view it would be better to settle the people and secure the borders, let the weapons sleep and renew the covenant, then broadly recruit outstanding men and move according to the times—that is the method for long endurance."
s0091.idiomatic: In my foolish view it would be better to settle the people and secure the borders, let the weapons sleep and renew the covenant, then broadly recruit outstanding men and move according to the times—that is the method for long endurance."

s0092.literal: Emperor Xuan did not follow him.
s0092.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan did not follow him.

s0093.literal: Later Wu Mingche was defeated by Zhou; Emperor Xuan told Xi: "What you said has been verified today."
s0093.idiomatic: Later Wu Mingche was defeated by Zhou; Emperor Xuan told Xi, "What you said has been verified today."

s0094.literal: In year 12 he was given additional Palace Attendant.
s0094.idiomatic: In year 12 he was given additional palace attendant.

s0095.literal: In year 13 he was appointed Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and Governor of Danyang.
s0095.idiomatic: In year 13 he was appointed scattered-cavalry regular attendant and governor of Danyang.

s0096.literal: He was promoted to Minister of the Masters of Writing for Personnel, regular attendant as before.
s0096.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of the masters of writing for personnel, regular attendant as before.

s0097.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, Shuling plotted treason; an order had Central Palace Attendant Lu Qiong proclaim the intent, ordering northern and southern armies alike to take Xi's disposition.
s0097.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan died, Shuling plotted treason; an order had central palace attendant Lu Qiong proclaim the intent, ordering northern and southern armies alike to take Xi's disposition.

s0098.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was again given additional Palace Attendant, his enfeoffment increased together with the previous to nine hundred households.
s0098.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified he was again given additional palace attendant, his enfeoffment increased together with the previous to nine hundred households.

s0099.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was appointed Trustworthy Prestige General and Interior Administrator of Yongjia, with additional stipend of middle two thousand piculs.
s0099.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhide (583) he was appointed trustworthy prestige general and interior administrator of Yongjia, with additional stipend of middle two thousand piculs.

s0100.literal: At first Emperor Xuan entrusted government to Xi; Xi also devoted his heart in loyal service, with much correction and benefit; he often remonstrated and his advice was followed—in more than ten years, though the Jiangdong realm was small, it was called fully flourishing.
s0100.idiomatic: At first Emperor Xuan entrusted government to Xi; Xi also devoted his heart in loyal service, with much correction and benefit; he often remonstrated and his advice was followed—in more than ten years, though the Jiangdong realm was small, it was called fully flourishing.
